motionPolicy.reason: Presentation surface, not a general-purpose web UI; motion is part of the CRT-phosphor identity and the explanation.
motionPolicy.fallback: Print stylesheet renders a static white-paper deck.

motionThesis.focalMoment: The pipeline signal and stage readout; the system check is the authored replay moment.
motionThesis.continuity: Progress segments and previous/next controls move between slides; the fixed CRT atmosphere stays continuous.
motionThesis.feedback: Node selection updates the stage readout; boot replay restarts the boot lines; record Replay restarts the record sequence.
motionThesis.budget: Transform, opacity, border, and background-position on the active slide; fixed atmosphere behind the reading column; no layout animation.

narrative.overview: The deck uses a CRT terminal world: near-black glass, phosphor and amber status colors, monospace telemetry, and a system-check panel on the cover. The visual language stays behind the argument. Motion is part of the presentation: the cover runs a short system check, the loop carries a moving packet, and the dataset and analysis diagrams scan continuously. The print stylesheet is the static fallback.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black glass with phosphor green and amber status roles.
A fixed CRT atmosphere: scanlines, vignette, rolling band, and a ghost GLASSHAND wordmark.
Square, rule-based panels; no rounded cards and no hard offset shadows.
Display type for the argument; monospace for data, labels, and terminal copy.
Rows, readouts, and a six-stage pipeline instead of a uniform card grid.
Ongoing loops: scanline sweep, pipeline signal, status lights, row and panel scans, and a breathing CRT vignette.
Interactive state: progress segments jump to slides, pipeline nodes select a stage, boot replay reruns the log, and record Replay restarts the record sequence.
No reduced-motion path: motion is part of the presentation, not optional chrome.
Diagrams use 1px instrument strokes, mono labels, phosphor for active/primary, and amber for boundaries or pending states.
Cover intro is sequenced: black mask, CRT power-on, with the initial system check starting as the power-on settles; returning to the cover restarts it immediately. The boot console is optional.
No pointer-following cursor or reticle: the deck is presented, not browsed.
Diagram surfaces: loop, record format, evidence map, analysis order, scope strip, and artifact chain. Each carries a relationship already stated in the slide.
Proposal-only language: PLANNED marks a specified stage; OPEN marks work not yet evidenced.
Ongoing motion: loop packet, pipeline beam, rail dot, dataset scan, evidence pulses, scope marker, and artifact scan.

rules.name: The Phosphor Rarity Rule
rules.body: Phosphor is a state, not a surface. Use it for active, measured, or verified things; let cream and body carry the reading. If phosphor is scattered as decoration, the signal dies.

rules.name: The One Screen Rule
rules.body: The ghost wordmark, scanlines, rolling band, and vignette are one atmospheric layer. Never add a second competing effect, a neon glow, or a gradient text treatment.

rules.name: The Data in Mono Rule
rules.body: Monospace is for data, labels, code, and terminal copy. It is not a costume for every line of prose; the display face carries the argument.

rules.name: The No Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: A heading carries its own weight. Course, status, and slide context live in the fixed top bar, not in a small kicker above the heading.

rules.name: The Flat Glass Rule
rules.body: If an element needs a shadow to separate itself, the rule or spacing is wrong. Fix the structure, not the depth.

rules.name: The Presentation Motion Rule
rules.body: Motion is part of the argument and the charm. Do not add a prefers-reduced-motion kill switch, do not freeze the CRT loops, and do not treat this deck as a general-purpose web interface. Keep loops slow, low-opacity, and behind or around the reading line; animate opacity, transforms, borders, and background scans rather than layout.

dos: Do keep phosphor for active/measured/verified states and amber for proposal/open states.
Do label every state with text ([ PLANNED ], [ OPEN ]), not color alone.
Do use a diagram when a slide has a structural relationship (loop, record format, evidence chain, analysis order, or scope) and a side column is empty; the diagram must carry the argument.
Do label every diagram with its boundary or state in text, not color alone.

Do sequence the cover intro: black mask, CRT power-on, with the initial system check starting as the power-on settles; returning to the cover restarts it immediately. The console is optional and must never be required for navigation.
Do keep loops slow and low-opacity; a scan may pass through a component, but it must never move the reading line.
donts: Don't add a metric, application name, result, or claim inside a diagram that is not already on the slide.
Don't add a prefers-reduced-motion path or freeze the CRT loops.
Don't add pointer-following reticles or custom cursor effects. This deck is presented, not browsed.
Don't fill white space with decorative cards or invented labels. If the content has no relationship to draw, leave the breathing room.
